text:
tori: Quick sync: DeltaRetail asked for a temporary 'surge-credit' pilot — 3 months, 3 bursts/month, up to 24h each. No extra commit. Need guardrails + billing language.

ben: TL;DR from sales: they want predictable billing and visibility. They'll accept best-effort latency on spilled requests but committed routes must keep SLOs.

ash: Engineering note: we can support a per-route `surge_credit` config with `max_hours`, `occurrences_per_month`, `max_tokens`, and `throttle_policy`. Runtime enforcement + metrics is straightforward.

lyn: Ops: must define deterministic throttle triggers. Proposed: start throttling burst when serving CPU>82% OR tail latency p99>800ms for >4min. Stop when both below thresholds for 6min.

opsbot: Added runbook stub: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-9450

ben: Finance wants a pilot floor. Proposal: first 2 bursts complimentary up to 200M tokens each, then on-demand rates. Also require a $1k/mo pilot fee to cover monitoring/exports.

ash: We should expose a `surge_credit.used` metric and Console counter so customers see remaining bursts. I'll emit events: surge.start/surge.end with tokens and route_id.

tori: Legal asked for a non-recalibration clause: "Surge events during the pilot will not be used to set long-term commit baselines." They want it in the addendum.

lyn: Also add a telemetry SLA: 24h accuracy on surge usage reporting or we can't reconcile billing.

ben: Sales asks: DeltaRetail wants one onboarding goodwill burst (4h) free. Ok?

nash: Fine for onboarding, but log it and don't change monthly floor.

tori: Action items: 1) Nash -> PR for `surge_credit` schema and events by Wed EOD. 2) Lyn -> run sim and validate throttle triggers by Thu. 3) Ben -> finalize pilot fee and billing phrase by Tue. 4) Tori -> coordinate legal addendum draft. I'll decide sign-off after sims.

ben: I'll draft billing line: "Two complimentary surge events per month up to 200M tokens each; subsequent surge usage billed at on-demand rates. Pilot fee $1000/mo. Redwood may apply reasonable protective measures to preserve system health."

tori: Legal prefers "reasonable protective measures" + explicit trigger refs. Good.

nash: Creating ticket INF-9450 and linking sim artifacts when ready.

opsbot: INF-9450 assigned to nash, lyn, ben — due 2026-05-12.
